court: Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction finality
issues.why: The court must confirm the remedial order and judgment are final/appealable or otherwise within appellate jurisdiction.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct review standards for summary judgment, constitutional/ADA rulings, and scope of injunctions.

issues.label: Proper party substitution
issues.why: The court must ensure the official-capacity defendant was properly substituted under Rule 25(d).

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment immunity
issues.why: The court must determine whether Ex parte Young permits the prospective relief sought against a state official and whether any relief is effectively retrospective.

issues.label: State sovereign immunity limits
issues.why: The court must assess whether any ordered reporting or operational mandates impermissibly intrude on state sovereignty beyond permissible federal equitable relief.

issues.label: Standing each plaintiff
issues.why: The court must confirm each plaintiff has injury in fact, causation, and redressability for each claim and each form of relief.

issues.label: Standing for each claim
issues.why: The court must evaluate standing separately for SNAP Act, Due Process, and ADA theories rather than globally.

issues.label: Standing for each remedy
issues.why: The court must determine whether plaintiffs have standing to seek each specific declaratory/injunctive provision (e.g., call-wait targets, facility constraints, grievance procedures).

issues.label: Organizational standing theory
issues.why: The court must decide whether Empower Missouri has direct organizational standing via diversion-of-resources or only associational standing.

issues.label: Diversion-of-resources injury
issues.why: The court must assess whether Empower’s expenditures are fairly traceable to DSS practices and not merely self-inflicted advocacy costs.

issues.label: Associational standing elements
issues.why: If asserted, the court must evaluate whether Empower’s members would have standing, the interests are germane, and individual participation is unnecessary.

issues.label: Taxpayer/generalized grievance bar
issues.why: The court must ensure Empower’s alleged harms are not generalized grievances about government performance.

issues.label: Mootness individual claims
issues.why: Because all individuals now receive benefits, the court must decide whether claims are moot and whether any exception applies.

issues.label: Voluntary cessation
issues.why: The court must determine whether DSS’s post-suit interviews/approvals moot claims or whether the challenged practices likely persist.

issues.label: Capable of repetition evading review
issues.why: The court must decide whether recurring recertification/application cycles make future harm likely yet too short to litigate fully.

issues.label: Ongoing injury likelihood
issues.why: The court must evaluate evidence that each individual faces a real and immediate threat of future denial or barriers.

issues.label: Ripeness of future harms
issues.why: The court must ensure claims for future application/recertification barriers are sufficiently imminent for adjudication.

issues.label: Redressability of injunction
issues.why: The court must determine whether the requested/ordered relief would likely prevent the asserted future injuries.

issues.label: Causation traceability
issues.why: The court must assess whether harms stem from Bax/DSS policies versus third-party factors (e.g., applicant errors, federal rules, call volume).

issues.label: Classwide-type relief without class
issues.why: The court must consider whether broad statewide injunctions are permissible in a non-class action based on these plaintiffs’ injuries.

issues.label: Private right under SNAP Act
issues.why: The court must decide whether 7 U.S.C. §§ 2014/2020 and regulations are enforceable by private plaintiffs and by what vehicle.

issues.label: Section 1983 enforceability
issues.why: The court must determine whether SNAP provisions create rights enforceable under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 (Blessing/Gonzaga framework) or are precluded by a comprehensive scheme.

issues.label: Supremacy Clause enforcement
issues.why: If §1983 is unavailable, the court must consider whether equitable preemption/Armstrong limits bar direct enforcement of the SNAP Act.

issues.label: Regulations enforceability
issues.why: The court must determine whether accompanying SNAP regulations independently create enforceable rights or can be enforced only through statutory rights.

issues.label: Agency waiver relevance
issues.why: The court must address the legal effect of DSS’s claimed federal waiver (recertification interviews) and the consequence of its absence from the record.

issues.label: Interpretation interview requirements
issues.why: The court must construe federal SNAP rules on interviews, scheduling, and the 30-day processing window and how they constrain state practices.

issues.label: Automatic denial policy legality
issues.why: The court must decide whether denying applications solely for non-completion of interview within 30 days regardless of applicant efforts violates federal law or due process.

issues.label: First-day application rule
issues.why: The court must interpret and apply 7 U.S.C. § 2020(e)(2)(B) requirements about allowing households to apply on the first day they contact DSS.

issues.label: What counts as contact
issues.why: The court must determine whether unanswered calls, menu prompts, or resource-center visits constitute “contact” triggering first-day application obligations.

issues.label: What counts as application filing
issues.why: The court must decide when an application is deemed filed/registered (including online submissions not registered) under federal law.

issues.label: Processing timeliness obligations
issues.why: The court must assess SNAP deadlines for acting on applications and how call-center failures affect compliance.

issues.label: Recertification process obligations
issues.why: The court must determine what procedural obligations apply at recertification (forms, interviews, verifications) and whether they differ from initial applications.

issues.label: Property interest in SNAP
issues.why: For due process, the court must determine whether applicants/recipients have a constitutionally protected property interest in benefits at application and recertification stages.

issues.label: Applicant vs recipient interests
issues.why: The court must distinguish due-process protections for initial applicants versus current recipients facing potential termination/non-renewal.

issues.label: Entitlement eligibility showing
issues.why: The court must assess whether plaintiffs were “otherwise eligible” such that denial for interview failure deprived them of an entitlement rather than a mere expectation.

issues.label: Procedural due process standard
issues.why: The court must apply Mathews v. Eldridge balancing to determine what process is due given the risk of erroneous deprivation and administrative burdens.

issues.label: Meaningful opportunity to be heard
issues.why: The court must decide whether DSS provided a meaningful chance to complete interviews and submit information before denial.

issues.label: Adequacy of notice
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether DSS notices about interview requirements, deadlines, and consequences were constitutionally adequate.

issues.label: Opportunity for in-person interview
issues.why: The court must decide whether refusing same-day in-person interviews at resource centers violates due process or federal requirements.

issues.label: Arbitrariness and consistency
issues.why: The court must consider whether inconsistent or arbitrary application handling (disconnects, non-registration, auto-denials) constitutes due-process violation.

issues.label: Causation of deprivation
issues.why: The court must determine whether any deprivation was caused by state action (systemic barriers) rather than plaintiffs’ failure to comply.

issues.label: Remedies for past due process harms
issues.why: The court must determine whether declaratory or prospective relief is appropriate given that past denials have been remedied by later approvals.

issues.label: ADA Title II applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether DSS is a public entity under Title II and whether official-capacity suit for prospective relief is proper.

issues.label: ADA elements satisfied
issues.why: The court must decide whether Holmes and Dallas are qualified individuals with disabilities and were excluded from or denied benefits/services by reason of disability.

issues.label: Causation 'by reason of'
issues.why: The court must determine whether barriers were disability-based discrimination versus general system failures affecting all applicants.

issues.label: Reasonable accommodation duty
issues.why: The court must assess whether DSS failed to make reasonable modifications or provide auxiliary aids/services necessary for meaningful access.

issues.label: Accommodation request sufficiency
issues.why: The court must decide whether Dallas’s note and Holmes’s circumstances constituted adequate requests or sufficient notice triggering an interactive duty.

issues.label: Interactive process relevance
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether ADA/Section 504 require an interactive process and whether DSS’s response was legally sufficient.

issues.label: Communication accessibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether phone-menu prompts, long holds, and disconnections deny effective communication for applicants with cognitive/neurological impairments.

issues.label: Program accessibility resource centers
issues.why: The court must determine whether DSS resource centers provided meaningful access (including interview availability) consistent with Title II program accessibility rules.

issues.label: Grievance procedure requirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether Title II regulations require ADA/Section 504 grievance procedures for DSS and whether plaintiffs have standing for that relief.

issues.label: Section 504 applicability
issues.why: Because plaintiffs seek Section 504-related relief, the court must address whether it is pled, available, and coextensive with ADA Title II here.

issues.label: Exhaustion requirements
issues.why: The court must determine whether any administrative exhaustion is required for ADA/Section 504 or SNAP-related claims seeking equitable relief.

issues.label: Qualified immunity inapplicable
issues.why: The court must confirm qualified immunity does not apply to official-capacity claims for prospective relief but consider any other defenses.

issues.label: Causation of non-registration
issues.why: The court must decide whether Davis’s first online application failure (incorrect SSN) is attributable to DSS and legally relevant to claims.

issues.label: Harmless error materiality
issues.why: The court must assess whether alleged applicant errors or missing information break the chain for liability or affect remedies.

issues.label: Summary judgment record sufficiency
issues.why: The court must decide whether undisputed facts establish liability or whether genuine disputes exist (e.g., efforts to interview, DSS capabilities, policies).

issues.label: Scope of district court findings
issues.why: The court must ensure the district court did not resolve credibility disputes or make improper fact findings at summary judgment.

issues.label: Systemic policy vs isolated acts
issues.why: The court must determine whether evidence shows an official policy/practice causing violations versus isolated implementation failures.

issues.label: Declaratory relief appropriateness
issues.why: The court must determine whether declaratory relief would resolve a live controversy and is not merely advisory given current benefit receipt.

issues.label: Permanent injunction prerequisites
issues.why: The court must ensure irreparable harm, inadequacy of legal remedies, balance of equities, and public interest requirements are satisfied.

issues.label: Injunction narrow tailoring
issues.why: The court must ensure relief is no broader than necessary to redress plaintiffs’ injuries (Rule 65 and equitable principles).

issues.label: Federalism/comity constraints
issues.why: The court must consider limits on federal courts supervising state agencies and avoid overly intrusive structural injunctions.

issues.label: Rule 65 specificity
issues.why: The court must assess whether injunction terms are specific and definite enough to provide clear notice of required conduct.

issues.label: Ongoing judicial supervision
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether monthly reporting to court and state officials constitutes improper continuing oversight beyond what equity permits.

issues.label: Reporting to legislature/executive
issues.why: The court must decide whether ordering filings to nonparties (state legislative/executive members) exceeds judicial authority or violates separation-of-powers principles.

issues.label: Numeric performance targets authority
issues.why: The court must determine whether imposing call-wait and denial-percentage quotas is authorized by the legal violations found and supported by the record.

issues.label: Causal link to targets
issues.why: The court must assess whether the chosen metrics (20-minute waits, 20% denials) are connected to remedying legal wrongs rather than policy preferences.

issues.label: Feasibility and compliance burden
issues.why: The court must consider whether ordered operational requirements are feasible and whether undue burden defenses apply (especially under ADA reasonableness).

issues.label: Modification of facility operations
issues.why: The court must decide whether enjoining changes to DSS facility hours/staffing is impermissibly broad or unsupported by plaintiffs’ injuries.

issues.label: Relief for already-interviewed Holmes
issues.why: The court must determine mootness/overbreadth of ordering an interview within three days for Holmes who later was interviewed and approved.

issues.label: Prospective relief for recertification
issues.why: The court must decide whether future recertification barriers justify injunction for Dallas whose benefits never lapsed.

issues.label: Attorneys' fees eligibility
issues.why: Although not described, the court must consider potential entitlement to fees/costs under §1988/ADA if relevant to judgment.

issues.label: Vacatur if moot on appeal
issues.why: If claims became moot, the court must consider whether to vacate the district court judgment under Munsingwear principles.

issues.label: Severability of remedies
issues.why: The court must determine whether any unlawful portions of the injunction can be severed while leaving valid relief intact.

issues.label: Remand for remedy tailoring
issues.why: If liability stands but remedy is overbroad, the court must decide whether to remand for revised injunction terms.
